root_idea.summary: The root denotes driving or pushing something forward, especially in a forceful, flowing movement.
root_idea.development: From this central idea develop the senses of pouring or gushing, a quantity released at once, overflow, and figurative rapid movement.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested active participle is presented under its normalized dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: Flowing or gushing rapidly and forcefully; also understood as poured forth.
senses.usage_conditions: In ماءٍ دافقٍ, describes the fluid as pouring out at once or with vehemence, as possessing a gush, or, in a recognized participial interpretation, as poured out.

senses.definition: Seminal fluid, in the Quranic interpretation of the fluid named in ماءٍ دافقٍ.
senses.usage_conditions: This is a Quran-specific interpretation of the expression in which the fluid is identified as seminal emission.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour liquid or contents out, especially at once or with vehemence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually transitive; an intransitive use with water or tears is reported, though its acceptability is disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To overflow or become full so that water pours forth from the sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a river, rivulet, or valley.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a beast hasten; of a beast, to hasten or go quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to beasts of conveyance and other animals described as moving rapidly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour out someone's spirit, meaning to cause that person to die; also used as an imprecation meaning “may he die.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or imprecatory construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to have its teeth projecting outward or its elbows spread apart from its sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily description of a camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause something to pour forth copiously or abundantly; figuratively, to bestow lavishly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The figurative use includes hands pouring forth largesse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour or flow forth copiously, or to become poured forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or quasi-passive derived construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hasten into false, vain, or unprofitable activity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction used with falsehood or vanity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For one's forbearance or clemency to depart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction describing the loss of self-restraint.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour forth or out, or to become poured forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive derived form, equivalent in this usage to flowing or being poured out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the contents of a mug to be poured forth or out at once.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said specifically of a vessel whose contents are released suddenly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act of pouring forth or out, whether at once or with vehemence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A countable occurrence or instance of pouring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quantity poured forth at once or with vehemence; a gush of rain or blood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The quantity may be a continuous fall or release without interruption.

other_classical_meanings.definition: All at once or together, especially of a group arriving as one body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional adverbial construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swift, quick, or fleet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a camel or horse, and to a camel's manner of going.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swift, fleet she-camel, particularly one of generous race.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An animal description; the source also associates the term with rapid movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that has never given birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate reported application of the same lexical form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A manner of walking or running quickly, sometimes with wide or alternating steps.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person's gait; the description can also refer to a swaying or uneven manner of proceeding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A torrent that fills a valley or its two sides; by extension, swift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective applied to a powerful, rapidly moving torrent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pouring forth copiously or abundantly; said of extensive, abundant rain and of a river or rivulet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also applied to the mouth of a leather water-bag that pours out abundantly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pouring forth abundantly; in دَافِقُ خَيْرٍ, pouring forth good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A prognosticatory expression used when the contents of a vessel are poured out.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick or swift in pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a pace or rate of going, including the utmost degree of the pace called العَنَق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bowed or bent in the back because of age or grief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a new moon, oblique; in another reported usage, upright and white rather than turned sideways.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources preserve differing applications of the adjective to the form and position of the new moon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having teeth projecting outward or forward; of a camel, having the elbows spread apart from its sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a camel or to a mouth, with the bodily description varying by object.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Core pouring meaning, including forceful release.
Pouring or scattering a vessel's contents is covered by the general transitive pouring meaning.
Transitive animal-speed usage is grouped with the corresponding intransitive usage.

cautions: The Quranic expression ماءٍ دافقٍ has several explicitly reported interpretations: rapidly gushing, poured forth, possessing a gush, and referring to seminal fluid.
The intransitive use of Form I with water or tears is reported but disputed in the lexical evidence.
